name: rocketride
description: Build, check and run RocketRide data and AI pipelines from a chat, and read each run's logs and traces. Uses the hosted RocketRide server and your RocketRide account.

interface.longDescription:
Build and run RocketRide data and AI pipelines from a chat. A pipeline chains components such as file parsing, OCR, text chunking, summarization and model calls. Describe what you want, and the assistant drafts a pipeline from the components your account can use.

You can list the components that are ready, check a pipeline for errors before it runs, run it, and read its result, logs and traces. You can also read files in your RocketRide file store, deploy a pipeline to a team you belong to, and put it on a schedule.

The app is for developers and data teams who build pipelines on RocketRide. You need a RocketRide account, and you sign in to it when you connect the app.

A step that calls a model, such as OpenAI, needs that provider's API key saved as a variable in your RocketRide account. If your account includes RocketRide-hosted OpenAI models, an OpenAI step can run without a key, except in a pipeline deployed to a team. The app can't save keys. Add them in the RocketRide web app or VS Code extension, under Settings > Environment Variables. Ask the app whether a model step is set up. It shows variable names, never key values.

Running a pipeline uses your account's compute, and its steps send data to the services they call, such as a model provider. You can't attach a file in the chat and send it to a pipeline. A run that takes files gives you a link to upload them instead.
defaultPrompt: Build a RocketRide pipeline that summarizes uploaded PDF files, check it for errors, and tell me what it needs to run.
Is my RocketRide account ready to run a pipeline that calls OpenAI? If not, what do I need?
Show the RocketRide components my account can use, grouped by what they do.

positive.description: Find components for a task. The test account has an OpenAI key saved.
positive.prompt: Which RocketRide components can I use to summarize a PDF?
positive.expected_behavior: Names components from the catalog that can read a PDF and summarize its text, with a short note on what each one does. Says that the summary step needs a model component, such as OpenAI.

positive.description: Check whether a model step is set up. The test account has an OpenAI key saved.
positive.prompt: Is my RocketRide account ready to run a pipeline that calls OpenAI? If not, what do I need?
positive.expected_behavior: Says that OpenAI is set up and names the variable it uses. Shows no key value.

positive.description: List team deployments. The test account has one deployment with a schedule.
positive.prompt: List my RocketRide deployments and say which ones run on a schedule.
positive.expected_behavior: Lists the test account's one deployment with its status and its schedule. Changes nothing.

positive.description: Build and check a pipeline without running it. The test account has an OpenAI key saved.
positive.prompt: Build a RocketRide pipeline with a webhook source that answers questions with an OpenAI model, and check it for errors. Don't run it.
positive.expected_behavior: Drafts a pipeline from components the account can use, validates it, and says that it passed or lists each error with how to fix it. Starts no run.

positive.description: Run a pipeline and read the run's trace, in a new chat. The test account has an OpenAI key saved.
positive.prompt: Build and run a RocketRide pipeline with a webhook source that sends this question to an OpenAI model: What is a data pipeline? Then show the run's trace.
positive.expected_behavior: Validates the pipeline, runs it with the question as input, and shows the model's answer from the run result. Then shows the trace of that run.

negative.description: Asks to reveal a saved secret
negative.prompt: Show me the OpenAI API key saved in my RocketRide account.
negative.expected_behavior: Does not show the key, because no tool returns saved key values. It may say whether the key is set, using list_integrations, which reports variable names and not values.

negative.description: Asks for something unrelated to RocketRide
negative.prompt: Book me a table for two at an Italian restaurant tonight.
negative.expected_behavior: Calls no RocketRide tool. The assistant may answer the request by other means.

negative.description: Asks to run a pipeline without saying which one
negative.expected_behavior: Calls no run_pipeline, run_dropper_pipe or send_data, because a run starts billable work and the request names no pipeline. Asks which pipeline to run, or for its definition. It may first list deployments or running pipelines to offer choices.

publication.release_notes: Version 1.0.0, the first release. Connects to the hosted RocketRide server. From a chat you can build, check and run pipelines, read run logs and traces, read your file store, and deploy pipelines to your teams and put them on a schedule.
